messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to fines and points. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Stop in both directions; reverse only if safe. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• No passing on the right unless the left lane is occupied. | Improper lane changes can lead to points. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone can result in a $50 fine. | | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Red‑light running, stop‑sign violations, and failure to obey traffic signals are punishable. | Fines range from $50–$200; points added. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points are removed after 2 years of no violations. | | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Higher coverage is recommended. | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | • Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles.
• Registration renewal is due annually; late fees apply. | | | **Special Situations** | • **Construction Zones**: Speed limits reduced, often 20 mph.
• **High‑way Exit/Entry**: Must use acceleration/deceleration lanes. | | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and updates. - **Local County Ordinances**: May impose additional restrictions (e.g., speed limits, parking rules). ### Quick Resources - **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – downloadable PDF. - **Texas.gov – Driver’s License & Vehicle Registration** – online portal. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – for enforcement and reporting. --- **Tip:** If you’re planning to drive in Texas, it’s a good idea to review the Texas Transportation Code sections relevant to your situation (e.g., commercial driving, school bus rules, or DUI). This will help you stay compliant and avoid penalties.
